liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Playing In The Band** (3 reviews, 1 other source): Reviewer finds this Playin' long and dreamy, with the latter part of the show very strong; Playin' contains early riffs of the 'Happiness is Drumming' idea, later the Fire on the Mountain instrumental [1][6][11][14]
- **Crazy Fingers** (3 reviews): First-set Crazy Fingers into Comes A Time is singled out as outstanding; Crazy Fingers into Comes A Time is called a powerful opening pairing [7][11][12]
- **Eyes Of The World** (2 reviews): Eyes was played at an uptempo pace, which fans nicknamed 'your Eyes on speed'; In Eyes, the jam takes over the band for roughly the first five minutes [8][12]
- **U.S. Blues** (1 review): Opening with U.S. Blues, Jerry played toward the flag and the crowd went wild [16]
- **Comes A Time** (1 review): On the other audience version, a loud scream is audible as Jerry begins his guitar break [9]
- **One More Saturday Night** (1 review): Reviewer points to the crowd noise during Around and Around and One More Saturday Night [6]

## Setlist highlights

- **Drums/Bass**: back after 187 archived shows (1363 days); rare: 3 archived performances [18]

## The recordings

- **gd1976-06-22.sbd.digitalrbb.miller.112218.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 22 songs; 187 min; rated 4.86/5 by 14 [1]
- **gd76-06-22.aud.vernon.6680.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 21 songs; 170 min; rated 4.4/5 by 5 [4]. Said about its sound: Audience recording rated 3.5 for sound quality, lower than the music; Reviewer thinks the audience recording's sound could be better; Reviewer finds the audience recording's sound quality really good [6][7][10]
- **gd1976-06-22.akg.moore.berger-minches.99093.flac16**: source not stated; 22 songs; 170 min; rated 2.67/5 by 3 [5]. Said about its sound: This Moore/Berger-Minches AKG version has less crowd noise than the other circulating version, which the reviewer finds distracting [9]
- **gd1976-06-22.mtx.seamons.112900.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 188 min; rated 3.75/5 by 4 [2]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended all four nights of this tour stretch and calls this their favorite; the energy was incredible [8]
- The Tower held 3500 people and had great acoustics, producing many quality audience tapes [8]
- Reviewer says 1976 had some of the coolest setlists the band played, and many good soundboards exist from that year [7]
- Setlist is more unorthodox than most of 1976, at the tail end of June [10]
- Attendee says ending the second set with Saturday Night on a Tuesday was never repeated; there was no encore [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1976-06-22.sbd.digitalrbb.miller.112218.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Cassette -> Apogee Ensemble -> Peak -> AIFF [1]. Also: Described as the first soundboard of this show on the archive, with audience patches mixed in smoothly; Soundboard was cleaned of static; patch source came from mics placed at the soundboard by a Dead crew member [1][11]
- **gd76-06-22.aud.vernon.6680.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording: Shure [4]
- **gd1976-06-22.akg.moore.berger-minches.99093.flac16**: taped by Jerry Moore; transferred by Rob Berger and David Minches; source: AKG D1000es>sony tc-152sd cassette [5]
- **gd1976-06-22.mtx.seamons.112900.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro (FLAC > AIFF > Soundtrack > Final Cut > AIFF CD tracking via Audacity > FLAC16 via xACT) [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Snooky Flowers Grateful Dead: [1976-06-22 Tower Theatre, Upper Darby, PA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1976-06-22-tower-theatre-upper-darby-pa-usa/) [23]
